# Sophaxis

> Sophaxis is an overlay preprint server for philosophy, mathematics, philosophy of mathematics, philosophy of science and logic. It lists preprints that authors have already deposited in an open repository with a DOI, and gives each a stable record page. Acceptance is moderation, not peer review. Sophaxis charges nothing, to authors or to readers.

The policies below are the rules. Where this file and a policy differ, the policy applies. The full text of every policy is in [llms-full.txt](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/llms-full.txt).

## Facts

- Operator: Takuya Nemoto (ORCID https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1406-0547), one person in Japan, unpaid. Requests by email go to the address on that ORCID record; see the [contact page](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/contact.html).
- Fields: Philosophy, Mathematics, Philosophy of Mathematics, Philosophy of Science, Logic.
- Accepted repositories (15): Zenodo, Figshare, OSF Preprints, SocArXiv, MetaArXiv, arXiv, Preprints.org, SSRN, Research Square, SciELO Preprints, Qeios, ScienceOpen Preprints, Advance, KC Works, Jxiv.
- Accepted licences: CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0, CC0 1.0.
- Records shown: 5 (removed records are not counted). 5 of the 5 records shown are the operator’s own submissions. The operator is at present the only moderator.
- Not offered in 43 places: the European Union, the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, China, Thailand, Russia, Türkiye, Egypt, Peru, Albania, Monaco, Guernsey, Botswana, Ecuador, Iraq, Indonesia, Rwanda, Zambia, Ethiopia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kazakhstan, Tunisia, Uganda, Guinea, Madagascar, Bolivia, Costa Rica and Quebec; and, from 2026-11-26, Argentina, Colombia, Ghana, Korea, Mexico, the Philippines, Saudi Arabia, Uruguay, Zimbabwe, Kenya, Tanzania, South Africa, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar. From 2026-11-22, a work is not listed if an author lives in one of them, or stays in one between the submission and the listing, even briefly. The [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html) gives the law of each.
- Age of the DOI: from 2026-11-23, a new work is listed only if at least 6 months have passed since its first DOI was registered, counted to the day the submission issue is opened.
- Changes announced on the top page, in effect since 2026-11-13 where the text says so, and otherwise from 2026-11-21 (where the text names a later day, that day): Since its publication on 2026-11-13, ahead of the changes below because going on would act against the terms of the two repositories, Sophaxis no longer copies PDFs by script from Figshare or Research Square, whose terms forbid robots and scripts; the authors of a work there can attach the deposited PDF to the submission issue instead. A person under 13 can no longer submit. A work with more than one author is listed only after every other author confirms their own agreement. Text written in the forms is shared under CC0 1.0, and an abstract given in a form under the licence of the work. The submission form asks two more confirmations: that every author consents to the record being published, offered through OAI-PMH and provided to services in the United States, and agreement to the policies. The form also asks for the extent of use of generative models, at one of four levels: none, editing, assistance or drafting. From 2026-11-22, a work is listed only if no author lives in a place where Sophaxis is not offered, as the Submission Policy lists them, or stays in one between the submission and the listing, even briefly, and no author under 18 lives or stays in India; the form asks the submitter to confirm it. The saves to the Internet Archive become a separate box that may be left empty. From 2026-11-23, a new work is listed only if, on the day its submission issue is opened, at least six months have passed since the first DOI of the work was registered; a new version of a listed work is not counted again. From the same day, a work for which Crossref records a retraction, a withdrawal or a removal is not listed, and one with an expression of concern goes to the operator first. From the same day, a submitter who is not yet an author of a listed work needs a researcher whose ORCID record lists a journal article, a book chapter or a book to vouch for it. From 2026-11-24, the form asks three more statements, on funding, on competing interests, and on human participants and research ethics, and a work is listed only if each is given; it also asks, optionally, where the data and code are. Confirming something untrue in a form is not allowed; from 2026-11-22, the operator may decline further submissions from the account that did so. From 2026-11-25, the court of first instance agreed in a form, for a dispute not settled by talks or mediation, is the Utsunomiya District Court or the Utsunomiya Summary Court, in place of the district court or the summary court that has jurisdiction over the operator's place of residence; the agreement stays non-exclusive, and the rights of consumers and of people outside Japan stay as they are. From 2026-11-26, that agreement on the court covers only suits based on the Terms of Use, or on the submission, listing, correction, withdrawal or removal of the person's own works under them; for any other dispute, the court that the law sets has jurisdiction. From 2026-11-26, Sophaxis is also not offered in 15 more places, and a work is not listed if an author lives in one of them, or stays in one between the submission and the listing: Argentina, Colombia, Ghana, Korea, Mexico, the Philippines, Saudi Arabia, Uruguay, Zimbabwe, Kenya, Tanzania, South Africa, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar. The reasons are laws read on 2026-11-12 that ask for registration, for conditions before personal data leaves the place, for the operator's postal address or telephone number before personal data is collected, or for a parent's consent that the service confirms before the data of a minor is processed, and data protection laws that could not be read at their source; the Submission Policy gives each. From 2026-11-26, in a dispute the operator aims to answer within 7 days rather than promising to, and during a pause described under "Continuity" in the Terms of Use the answer waits until the pause ends; the call for advisers says the same of its messages. From 2026-11-29, Sophaxis is also not offered in a place where the operator judges that offering Sophaxis would not conform to the law of that place; when the operator so judges, the place and the reason are added to the table of the Submission Policy, and the change to the table is announced on this page before it takes effect. From 2026-12-01, for a submission made on or after that day, the Terms of Use limit the operator's liability for loss caused by negligence that is not gross negligence to the loss that would ordinarily arise, never for intent or gross negligence and never toward a reader who has not agreed to them; and the submitter undertakes that each confirmation in the form is true and, after being told of a third party's claim and heard, compensates the operator for the loss that an untrue one causes, as Articles 415 and 416 of Japan's Civil Code provide.

## Policies

- [Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html): The rules for everyone who reads or submits.
- [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html): Who can submit what, and what the submitter confirms.
- [Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html): What moderation checks, and what it does not.
- [Copyright Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/copyright.html): Authors keep their copyright; what Sophaxis copies and why.
- [Licence Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/licences.html): The accepted licences, and the licences of this site.
- [Privacy Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/privacy.html): What the site and the checks read, and what becomes public.
- [Withdrawal Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/withdrawal.html): How an author withdraws a listed work, and what stays.
- [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html): How to ask for removal, and what happens then.
